reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.106.1-Ps.106.3 in an identity psalm: web_mt_offset_map gives Ps 106 rule identity with 48 verses in both witnesses, verse_map_web carries no Ps.106.0 title pseudo-verse, so no title-evidence question and no dual-cite arithmetic hazard arises here. Hebrew re-derived, not trusted: the v1 quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.106.1 and is character-for-character the entire verse (68 chars quoted, 68 in the source), so the Hebrew quote and its WEB gloss cover the same span. Both device claims re-checked against psalm_device_inventory.json rather than the row: halleluyah.verse_initial lists Ps.106.1 among its 11 entries, and hodu_openings holds exactly 6 entries (Ps.33.2, Ps.105.1, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1, Ps.118.29, Ps.136.1) with Ps.106.1 absent — the row's figure of 6 verse-initial hodu openings book-wide and its negative are both exact, and it correctly declines to treat the in-verse hodu as a frame opener. Word-position re-derived from the consonantal token list of MT 106:1: hallelu(1), yah(2), hodu(3), so 'third word' holds. The closing 3|4 seam is a byte-checkable person shift — זָכְרֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.106.4) and פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ps.106.4), both byte tier, carry 1cs object suffixes, against v1's two 2mp imperatives, v2's interrogative pair and v3's ashre beatitude. Disclosure obligations checked and none missed: pmarks_Ps.json records no selah anywhere in Ps 106, and its ketiv/qere list holds only Ps.106.45, outside every verse this row quotes; a paseq seg is inventoried at Ps.106.1 but the row makes no seg-layer claim, and paseq is not quotable verse text in any case. Tiling of Ps.106.1-Ps.106.27 across the cluster is exact (27 of 27 verses, no gaps or overlaps). Observation, not filed: rejected_alternative rejects a mid-verse split that the tiling rule forecloses anyway, so it never engages the live rival (a 1-2 / 3 cut, or a 1-5 merge); confidence high is nonetheless carried by the v4 suffix evidence.

Span Ps.106.4-Ps.106.5. The original-language core of the row is sound: זָכְרֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.106.4) collates at byte tier and is a 2ms imperative bearing a 1cs object suffix, matched by פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ps.106.4), byte tier, in the same verse; the three-fold lamed-infinitive quote at oshb:Ps.106.5 collates at byte tier as an ellipsis-ordered run and the count of three is right, WEB rendering all three 1cs, “that I may see the prosperity of your chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that I may glory with your inheritance.” (web:Ps.106.5). Both seams hold: 3|4 is the 1cs suffix shift, 5|6 the shift to 1cp perfects. Two defects, neither touching the span. First, the substrate signal attributes plural imperatives to vv1-2; MT 106:2 has no imperative, its two finite verbs being prefix-conjugation forms under the interrogative, and the only 2mp imperatives in the overture stand in v1. Second, those two verses are argued in prose outside the span but appear in no boundary_evidence_refs entry. Confidence high survives both — the person evidence at the opening seam is byte-checkable and independent of the mis-stated v2 form.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal credits vv1-2 with plural imperatives, but MT 106:2 contains no imperative at all; the overture's only 2mp imperatives both stand in MT 106:1.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collated at byte tier: MT 106:1 supplies both imperatives, הַֽלְלוּ (oshb:Ps.106.1) and הוֹד֣וּ (oshb:Ps.106.1). MT 106:2's two finite verbs are יְ֭מַלֵּל (oshb:Ps.106.2) and יַ֝שְׁמִ֗יעַ (oshb:Ps.106.2), byte tier, both carrying a yod preformative and both governed by the interrogative that opens the verse; the v1 pair carries no prefix consonant. Enumeration rather than assertion, with the unit named: MT 106:1 runs to 9 tokens and MT 106:2 to 7 tokens, and the two forms quoted here are the whole of v2's finite verbal stock — there is no third candidate to be an imperative. The staged extract has no morphology layer, so the form is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses, and WEB renders v2 as a question, not a command: “Who can utter the mighty acts of Yahweh, or fully declare all his praise?” (web:Ps.106.2), against v1's commands “Praise Yahweh! Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.” (web:Ps.106.1). The parallel treatment of the Ps.106.1-Ps.106.3 span in this same cluster reads the two verses distributively as imperative form in v1 and question form in v2, which is the correct description; this row collapses the pair into plural imperatives across both verses.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.106.6-Ps.106.6, a single-verse row in the full X-X form. The quote is clean: חָטָ֥אנוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6), הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6) and הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6) are all 1cp perfects, the quoted run collates at byte tier and is the entire verse (52 chars quoted, 52 in the source), and the WEB gloss “We have sinned with our fathers. We have committed iniquity. We have done wickedly.” (web:Ps.106.6) covers exactly the same span. No selah and no ketiv/qere touch this verse (pmarks_Ps.json lists Ps.106.45 as the psalm's only K/Q). Two original-language defects. First, a consonantally identical catchword straddles the row's own 6|7 seam and is nowhere disclosed, while the row's stated warrant for isolating the verse is that it names nothing — and its rejected_alternative is precisely the merge that catchword supports. Second, the person-grammar signal is false: it places a first-person plural return inside the petition and denies a person-shift at the row's opening seam, when MT 106:4-5 is 1cs throughout and 5|6 is exactly a 1cs-to-1cp shift — the same shift the Ps.106.4-Ps.106.5 span relies on for its own closing warrant, so the seam pair disagrees with itself about one seam. Neither challenge asks for the span to move: the confession genuinely differs in referent-class from the named recital, and confidence high is defensible on the span itself.

challenges.claim: A consonantally identical catchword straddles the row's own 6|7 seam undisclosed, and the rejected_alternative it bears on is answered without engaging it.
challenges.evidence: The word for 'our fathers' stands as the third-from-last token of MT 106:6, אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6), and as the FIRST token of MT 106:7, אֲב֘וֹתֵ֤ינוּ (oshb:Ps.106.7); both are spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and each collates at byte tier against its own verse. Tier named per discipline: the two are NOT byte-identical — the v6 token carries U+0597 and the v7 token carries U+0598 with U+05A4 — but they are identical at accent_stripped tier and at skeleton tier. Sweep with the object named first (plene consonantal spelling, verse counts): that spelling occurs in 5 verses book-wide — Ps.44.2, Ps.78.3, Ps.78.5, Ps.106.6, Ps.106.7 — and the defective spelling of the same word occurs in 1 verse, Ps.22.5. Inside Ps 106 the word therefore occurs in exactly 2 verses, and they are the two verses on either side of this seam. Both witnesses carry the link: “We have sinned with our fathers.” (web:Ps.106.6) is picked up at once by “Our fathers didn't understand your wonders in Egypt.” (web:Ps.106.7). Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed; here the row instead asserts that the confession names no place or event, and rejects attaching 106:6 to the Egypt and Red Sea episode without engaging the one signal that supports that rival. The ask is disclosure, not a merge, and the seam-pair cure is one edit installed on both this row and the Ps.106.7-Ps.106.12 row in the same pass.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal denies a person-shift at the row's opening seam and locates a first-person plural return inside the petition, but MT 106:4-5 carries no first-person plural form and 5|6 is a 1cs-to-1cp shift.

Visit me with your salvation,” (web:Ps.106.4). MT 106:5's three lamed-infinitives are rendered first-person singular throughout, “that I may see the prosperity of your chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that I may glory with your inheritance.” (web:Ps.106.5); across MT 106:4's 6 tokens and MT 106:5's 9 tokens — 15 tokens, enumerated, not sampled — no first-person plural form occurs at all. This verse's three verbs חָטָ֥אנוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6), הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6) and הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ (oshb:Ps.106.6) are 1cp, byte tier, and WEB matches: “We have sinned with our fathers.” (web:Ps.106.6). So the 5|6 boundary is a person-shift, and the closing warrant stated for the Ps.106.4-Ps.106.5 span says so — the plea's singular voice giving way to the confession's plural voice at that verse boundary. observed_substrate_signals is a driver-dependent field, so a signal that both invents a plural return in vv4-5 and denies the shift at the seam is a material evidence defect even though the one-verse span survives.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.106.7-Ps.106.12. Everything I could re-derive in the row's own evidence checks out. The v7 quote collates at byte tier as an ellipsis-ordered run against oshb:Ps.106.7, and the v9 quote at byte tier against oshb:Ps.106.9. The Red Sea recurrence claim is exact on an independent sweep: the two-token sea-name phrase, spliced from MT 106:22 and swept at skeleton tier, occurs in 5 verses book-wide — Ps.106.7, Ps.106.9, Ps.106.22, Ps.136.13, Ps.136.15 — so within this episode it stands at v7 and v9 exactly as claimed. The v12 close and the v13 opening are different response-classes on both witnesses, “Then they believed his words. They sang his praise.” (web:Ps.106.12) against “They soon forgot his works. They didn't wait for his counsel,” (web:Ps.106.13), so the 12|13 seam and the rejected 11|12 rival are handled correctly. No selah in Ps 106 and no K/Q in any verse this row quotes. The one defect is at the row's OPENING seam: the first word of MT 106:7 repeats the last content word of MT 106:6 consonant-for-consonant, an undisclosed continuity signal across the row's own boundary. That is the same seam defect the Ps.106.6 row carries, and by the seam-pair rule it is one repair authored once and installed on both rows in the same pass; I file it on both so neither can be cured alone. Confidence high stands: v7's naming of Egypt and the sea is the strongest tier-1 opener available here, and the challenge asks only for disclosure.

Sweep, object named first (plene consonantal spelling, verse counts): 5 verses book-wide, Ps.44.2, Ps.78.3, Ps.78.5, Ps.106.6, Ps.106.7; the defective spelling occurs in 1 verse, Ps.22.5. The cross-seam cohesion rule makes an undisclosed byte-true device straddling the row's seam an argument for continuity against the row; disclosure is the cure, one edit installed on both this row and the Ps.106.6 row, and the span itself should not move.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.106.13-Ps.106.15. The v14 quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.106.14 and the cognate-doubling claim is verifiable from the pointed bytes without a morphology layer: the verb and the noun immediately following it share the same three consonants under different prefixation, and WEB renders the figure “but gave in to craving in the desert, and tested God in the wasteland.” (web:Ps.106.14). Opening seam 12|13 is a response-class reversal on both witnesses; closing seam 15|16 is the entry of human proper names at v16. Neither seam leans on anything I could not re-derive, and the row cites no selah, no mark layer, no acrostic and no ketiv/qere — correctly, since pmarks_Ps.json puts no selah in Ps 106 and its only K/Q at Ps.106.45. Every verse argued lies inside the span, so the refs mirror is clean here. Two observations, neither filed. First, the signal that no personal name occurs in this episode is true only for human proper names: the pointed divine designation אֵ֝֗ל (oshb:Ps.106.14), byte tier, stands in v14, and per the short-token homography hazard I checked it by pointed bytes rather than by a consonantal count — it is the divine name, tsere-pointed, and WEB renders it “tested God in the wasteland” (web:Ps.106.14). The contrast the row draws is with Moses and Aaron, so the class is recoverable, but the wording leaves it implicit. Second, this is one of five span-scoped negative claims in the cluster that check_universals warns about for lacking a digit-bearing sweep; I verified each against the pointed bytes and none is false. Confidence medium is calibrated correctly for a three-verse episode whose seams rest on referent-class rather than on a formula.

Span Ps.106.16-Ps.106.18. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.106.16 and oshb:Ps.106.17, and the naming claim is right on the bytes: two lamed-prefixed personal names in v16 and two more names in v17, against no human proper name in vv13-15 or vv19-23. The 15|16 and 18|19 seams both hold — v19 opens on a place name where v16 opened on persons — and the row is correct that the following episode's opener is a place rather than a person. No selah, no K/Q, no mark-layer claim, nothing to disclose that was missed. The one defect is an evidence-array one: the three verses of the preceding episode are argued in the substrate signal but are mirrored by no refs entry. Observation, not filed: the phrase that the craving episode lacks that naming density entirely is an unswept zero-claim (check_universals flags it) and holds only for human proper names, since the pointed divine designation אֵ֝֗ל (oshb:Ps.106.14), byte tier, stands in v14; I leave it unfiled because the object class is recoverable from the row's own contrast and the claim is true under it. Confidence medium is right.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.106.24-Ps.106.27. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.106.24 and oshb:Ps.106.26. The oath handling is the strongest original-language work in the cluster: the row quotes the two-token idiom at v26 and glosses it transparently as a lifted hand meaning an oath, rather than letting WEB's “Therefore he swore to them that he would overthrow them in the wilderness,” (web:Ps.106.26) stand as if it were the Hebrew's surface sense — that is exactly the disclosure the argument needs when it leans on an English rendering. Opening seam 23|24 and closing seam 27|28 both sit at new-referent openers, and the closing signal is true on the bytes: MT 106:27 carries no proper name, while the next episode names a cult site at v28 and a person at v30. The internal repetition of the same infinitive across v26 and v27 is row-internal cohesion and argues for the span, not against it. No selah, no K/Q, no mark-layer or acrostic claim, and every verse argued lies inside the span, so the refs mirror is clean. Confidence medium is right for a four-verse unit whose interior could arguably be cut again at 25|26 between the rebellion and the sworn judgment; the rejected_alternative addresses the backward merge instead, which is the weaker rival, but that is a preference, not a defect.
